recentItems.title: Bangladesh tribunal orders 3 journalists held until trial in 2024 uprising case
recentItems.description:
(24 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Dhaka, Bangladesh – 24 August 2026
1. Wide of police escorting  arrested journalists Shyamal Dutta and  Mozammel Babu to court building
2. Mid of police escorting arrested journalist Farzana Rupa to court building
3. Various of International Crimes Tribunal gate  
4. Wide of exterior of International Crimes Tribunal building 
5. Motorcade of the International Crimes Tribunal judge outside court
6. SOUNDBITE (Bangla) Faruque Ahmed, International Crimes Tribunal Bangladesh prosecutor: 
“They have been accused of involvement in the events surrounding the mass uprising, including allegedly inciting and assisting in those events. The honorable court had earlier ordered that they be brought before the court. In accordance with that order, the three accused appeared before the court today."
7. Various of police escorting arrested journalists Farzana Rupa and Shyamal Dutta from tribunal building to prison van 
8. Wide of police prison van leaving tribunal premises 
STORYLINE:
A special tribunal in Bangladesh’s capital on Monday asked authorities to keep three journalists jailed until their trial in a case involving a mass uprising that ousted former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina from office in 2024, lawyers said.  

During the student-led uprising, hundreds of people were killed, and Hasina was later sentenced to death on charges of crimes against humanity. She fled to India two years ago and was tried in absentia.

The tribunal asked that Mozammel Babu, editor-in-chief of private Ekattor Television, its principal correspondent Farzana Rupa and Shyamal Dutta, editor of daily Bhorer Kagoj and former general secretary of the National Press Club in Dhaka, remain jailed.

After they appeared before the tribunal on Monday, the judge fixed Oct. 25 for the next court proceedings and asked the investigators to submit their findings against the journalists.  

Global human rights groups have criticized the jailing of the journalists and the denial of bail, asking the government to drop the charges against them and stop criminalizing news reporting.

Prosecutors allege the three journalists incited the suppression of student demonstrators during the uprising. They say that the journalists asked Hasina provocative questions at a press conference on July 14, 2024, that led her to make disparaging remarks about the demonstrators before launching a bloody crackdown on the protesters leading to hundreds of deaths.

The three journalists have been in custody for years following Hasina’s ouster as they face various charges including murder involving the uprising in July-August 2024. They were arrested during an interim government headed by Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus who handed over power in February to a new government.

The families of the journalists complained that they were held illegally.  

“Launching a crimes-against-humanity case against journalists Shyamal Dutta, Mozammel Babu, and Farzana Rupa for simply asking questions at a press conference is outrageous and deeply troubling,”  Kunal Majumder, CPJ’s Asia-Pacific Program Coordinator,  said in a statement earlier this month.

He added that “editorial decisions may be partisan or ethically questionable, but they cannot be criminalized. Criminalizing editorial judgment sets a dangerous precedent and undermines Bangladesh’s reputation as a democracy. Authorities must immediately release the three journalists and drop the charges.”


AP Video by Al Emrun Garjon

ASSOCIATED PRESS - NO ACCESS ISRAEL MEDIA, PERSIAN-LANGUAGE TV STATIONS BASED OUTSIDE IRAN, BBC PERSIAN, VOA PERSIAN, MANOTO TV, OR IRAN INTERNATIONAL TV
Tehran, Iran - 24 August 2026
1. Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei arriving for regular briefing
2. Wide of journalists raising hands 
3. Wide of briefing
4. SOUNDBITE (Farsi) Esmail Baghaei, Iran's foreign ministry spokesman:
"The United States, the very country that was supposed to come to the aid of the Iranian people, is now using every tool at its disposal to punish them for one reason alone: because they insist on upholding their national sovereignty, independence, dignity, and self-respect."
5. Wide of media and cameras 
6. Wide of briefing
7. SOUNDBITE (Farsi) Esmail Baghaei, Iran's foreign ministry spokesman:
"Any complicity with the United States in carrying out its aggressive actions against Iran will certainly have consequences. Even now, the naval blockade of Iran amounts to an act of aggression. Any escalation of this situation will undoubtedly bring about consequences of its own. Our hands are not tied in the face of such aggressive actions. Under international law, other countries are also not permitted to go along with or cooperate with the United States, because everyone knows that these actions are in clear violation of international rules, international law, and human rights."
8. Wide of briefing
9. SOUNDBITE (Farsi) Esmail Baghaei, Iran's foreign ministry spokesman:
"We certainly did not start this war, but we will not allow it to end on terms dictated by the aggressor."
10. Close of journalist writing notes
11. Journalist writing notes
12. SOUNDBITE (Farsi) Esmail Baghaei, Iran's foreign ministry spokesman:
"Definitely, trying out methods that have already proven to be failures will certainly not bring about a different outcome. It will only show the extent of the hostility and resentment the United States holds toward each and every Iranian, because it knows full well that it is ordinary Iranian citizens who are affected by these sanctions."
13. Journalist asking question
14. Wide of briefing
STORYLINE:
Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson on Monday warned that Tehran would respond harshly to expanded U.S. sanctions, including measures against countries it sees as cooperating with Washington.

“Any escalation of this situation will undoubtedly bring about consequences,” Esmail Baghaei said. “Our hands are not tied.”

The prospect of expanded sanctions and Iran’s threat to respond come after weeks of impasse, with the United States having not yet dislodged Iran’s grip on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian attacks and threats have severely hampered traffic through the waterway, through which a fifth of the world’s traded oil passed before the war started nearly six months ago.


Sanctions have historically raised the prices of basic goods in Iran, but after years withstanding them, Iran’s economy has adapted through finding new trading partners and building domestic industries. 





AP video by Mohsen Ganji

recentItems.title: China’s Xi welcomes Jordan’s King Abdullah II in Beijing
recentItems.description:
(24 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTIONS SUMMARY:

AGENCY POOL
Beijing, China -  24 August 2026
1. Wide of Chinese President Xi Jinping and Jordanian King Abdullah II walking onto stage
2. Wide of welcome ceremony
3. Close of Xi and Abdullah
4. Wide of guards of honor
5. Wide of Xi and Abdullah
6. Various of Xi and Abdullah inspecting guards of honor
7. Xi and Abdullah smiling and waving at children   
8. Various of bilateral meetings 
9. Various of signing ceremony, Xi and Abdullah witnessing signing of documents 
10. Zoom out of Xi and Abdullah shaking hands 
STORYLINE:
Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomed Jordanian King Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein in Beijing on Monday, as the Jordanian monarch wrapped up his seven-day visit to China.

Xi held a welcome ceremony for Abdullah at the Great Hall of the People, followed by bilateral talks and a signing ceremony of cooperation documents.

During the meeting, Xi described the China-Jordan bilateral relationship as "a vivid example" of win-win cooperation between countries with different social systems and different sizes. 

China is ready to enhance strategic mutual trust, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation, and strengthen coordination and collaboration on multilateral platforms with Jordan so as to promote greater development of the strategic partnership between the two countries, Xi said. 

Abdullah expressed respect for China's model of development and economic growth, as well as its leadership on the international stage. 

He said the two sides had held in-depth discussions on deepening cooperation across a wide range of vital fields, including agriculture, technology, pharmaceuticals, tourism, education, and culture during his stay. 

On regional issues, Abdullah said Jordan and China are aligned on the need to achieve "comprehensive calm and stability" in the Middle East, so that the region's people can live in peace and prosperity. 

The two leaders witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents in areas such as diplomacy, trade and economy, industrial and supply chains, and the judiciary.

The king’s talks with Xi came after he visited Shanghai and Shenzhen, where he said he explored opportunities to deepen economic cooperation with China.

recentItems.title: Iran’s rial currency hits new record low as US prepares to announce more sanctions
recentItems.description:
(24 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY: NO ACCESS ISRAEL MEDIA, PERSIAN-LANGUAGE TV STATIONS BASED OUTSIDE IRAN, BBC PERSIAN, VOA PERSIAN, MANOTO TV, OR IRAN INTERNATIONAL TV

++THE ASSOCIATED PRESS IS ADHERING TO IRANIAN LAW THAT STIPULATES ALL MEDIA ARE BANNED FROM PROVIDING ISRAEL MEDIA, PERSIAN-LANGUAGE TV STATIONS BASED OUTSIDE IRAN, BBC PERSIAN, VOA PERSIAN, MANOTO TV AND IRAN INTERNATIONAL ANY COVERAGE FROM IRAN, AND UNDER THIS LAW IF ANY MEDIA VIOLATE THIS BAN THE IRANIAN AUTHORITIES CAN IMMEDIATELY SHUT DOWN THAT ORGANISATION IN TEHRAN++

ASSOCIATED PRESS  - NO ACCESS ISRAEL MEDIA, PERSIAN-LANGUAGE TV STATIONS BASED OUTSIDE IRAN, BBC PERSIAN, VOA PERSIAN, MANOTO TV, OR IRAN INTERNATIONAL TV
Tehran, Iran -  24 August 2026
1. Tilt up of poster with pictures of Iranian gold coins and U.S dollar bills
2. Pedestrians walking past currency exchange shops
3. Various of pedestrians
4. Sign reading (Farsi) "Currency, coin and mobile phone marketplace"
5. Various of digital display showing exchange rates
6. SOUNDBITE (Farsi) Mohammad Soofi, 55, Tehran resident:
"The (U.S dollar exchange) rate keeps going up, it's crossing 2,000,000 rials. The rate is fluctuating. It changes every moment."
7. Pedestrians and exchange shops
8. Picture of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Iran's former supreme leader
9. Pedestrians outside exchange shop
10. Various of digital display showing rates
11. SOUNDBITE (Farsi) Ahmad Mehrabi, 35, Tehran resident:
"Well this (depreciating Rial) is shrinking people's dinner tables. They (authorities) say it has no impact, but how's that even possible? We are feeling the effect with every fiber of our being."
12. Pedestrians
13. SOUNDBITE (Farsi) Ahmad Mehrabi, 35, Tehran resident:
"Well these sanctions are unfair, everybody knows that. (The U.S.) is an economic superpower. We people must support each other."
14. Pedestrians entering and exiting metro station
15. Picture of Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, Iran's former supreme leader
16. Traffic on road

STORYLINE:
Iran’s currency hit a record low Monday as Washington prepared to announce new sanctions it said would add further pressure on an economy already battered by previous sanctions and a U.S. naval blockade.

The rial dropped to 2.02 million to the U.S. dollar as trading opened on currency markets. 

Iran’s official Central Bank rate stood at around 1.5 million rial to the dollar, but the market rate is what most Iranians pay.

The currency had already been under pressure before the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28, as Iran faced double-digit inflation and negative growth, but has repeatedly hit new lows as nearly six months of war have taken an even greater toll.

Iranians find daily staples increasingly unaffordable. Since the war began, rice is up some 60% and prices of beef are more than 150% higher. 

Ahmad Mehrabi, a 35-year-old resident of Tehran, said that despite the government downplaying the impact of the falling currency, it is being felt by everyday Iranians. 

"Well this (depreciating Rial) is shrinking people's dinner tables. They (authorities) say it has no impact, but how's that even possible?" said Mehrabi. "We are feeling the effect with every fiber of our being." 

The International Monetary Fund forecasts that GDP will contract more than 5%.

Still, economic pressure has not yet translated into political pressure. 


The war, as a result, has devolved into a fight over who controls the strait, through which a fifth of the world’s traded oil transited before the conflict. Iran is now refusing to fully reopen it unless it can charge ships.

recentItems.title: Assad-era's grand mufti sentenced to life in prison by court in Damascus
recentItems.description:
(24 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Damascus, Syria - 24 August 2026
1. Tilt down of building of Palace of Justice in Damascus 
2. Syria flag on top of the Palace of Justice, where the trial is taking place
3. Various of Former grand mufti Ahmad Badreddine Hassoun sitting in a cell inside the courtroom
4. Wide of panel of three judges, sitting to announce the final verdict
5. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Judge Fakhreddine al-Aryan, head of the Fourth Criminal Court in Damascus:
“The court unanimously rules as follows in the name of the Arab people of Syria: First, the defendant, Ahmad Badreddine Hassoun, son of Muhammad Adib and his mother Hamida, born in 1949, is found guilty of the felony of an assault intended to incite civil war and sectarian conflict, punishable under Article 298, in conjunction with Article 216, of the General Penal Code. Accordingly, he is sentenced to life imprisonment. Second, he was convicted of the felony of incitement to intentional murder, punishable under Article 533, in conjunction with Article 216 of the General Penal Code, and was sentenced for this offense to 20 years’ imprisonment."
6. Mohammad al-Ali, a private complainant against Ahmad Hassoun UPSOUND (Arabic): “He was justifying and falsifying all the actions of the former regime. We reject this ruling and will demand his execution, and we will pursue this matter, God willing.”
7. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Mohammad al-Ali, a private plaintiff against Hassoun:
“This man legitimized the actions of the former regime in every move and every step. The head of the former regime was sentenced to death, so it is only fitting that they receive the same death sentence. This man should face the same death sentence as Bashar Hafez Ali Suleiman al-Wahsh (Bashar al-Assad), his brother Maher, and his defense minister, who carried out the bombing. This man legitimized and justified the bombing in Syria.”
8. Sign at the courtroom door reading in Arabic, “The hall of the Fourth Criminal Court” 
9. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Attorney Mohammad Salameh, Deputy Head of the Syrian Bar Association:
“The ruling stated in its substance that the grave crimes committed by the convicted criminal Ahmad Badreddine Hassoun constitute war crimes and crimes against humanity, which are not covered by any amnesty and are not subject to any statute of limitations. Therefore, Ahmad Badreddine Hassoun will spend the rest of his life in prison once the ruling is upheld by the Court of Cassation, God willing.”
10. Various of security members inside judiciary palace in Damascus
STORYLINE:
A former Islamic religious leader was sentenced to life in prison on Monday in the latest Syrian court trial of officials affiliated with the rule of ex-President Bashar Assad.

Former grand mufti Ahmad Badreddine Hassoun, an Assad loyalist who was vocally in support of the government’s policies, was convicted of inciting violence and justifying murder. 

He held the position of mufti from 2005 to 2021, when the position was abolished.

Several other senior Assad-era officials -- including Assad himself and his brother, Maher -- have been sentenced to death in recent weeks, many of them in absentia. 

Hassoun was in custody and present in the court.

Some human rights groups have expressed concerns that the trials are being rushed and are potentially unfair, but the sentences have been welcomed by many Syrians who had previously expressed frustration that the new government was not moving with enough speed or strength against Assad-era figures.



AP Video by Ghaith Alsayed

“Do you see how many people have gathered? Members of many clubs and teams have come here to show their support. This is not a competition. There is no winner, and it does not matter who swims faster. The important thing is to participate and unite as one.”

14. SOUNDBITE (Ukrainian) Yevhenii Lakhnenko, 46, Ukraine army serviceman:  
"We are fighting for it at a heavy cost. We have fought, we are still fighting and I think we will have to continue fighting for our independence for many years to come. I am truly proud of our country and above all, of our people. I do not think there is another country in the world as strong as Ukraine. Only our people are capable of doing what we are doing.”
15. Mid of prosthetics on the sand
16. SOUNDBITE (Ukrainian) Yevhenii Lakhnenko, 46, Ukraine army serviceman: 
"I was wounded on 9 October 2025. I have recovered. As you can see, I swam a long distance today, which is very good. Swimming is what helped me, and what you see today is because of swimming. 17. Mid of Maksym Yuzviak, 35, Ukraine army serviceman, at Iron Week 
18. SOUNDBITE (Ukrainian) Maksym Yuzviak, 35, Ukraine army serviceman: 
“I was an operator of strike drones that we call Baba Yaga. Those are  large  bombs. I was wounded in January 2025. You could say I was unlucky when I got out of the trench. The enemy identified our position and launched a drone attack. One of the drones fell at my feet.”
18. Close of prosthetics
19.  SOUNDBITE (Ukrainian) Maksym Yuzviak, 35, Ukraine army serviceman: 
"Independence is the people — people who are ready to take responsibility and who, as they say, are capable of taking action.”
20. Wide of participants holding flags
21. Mid of amputee being assisted to chair
22. Wide of participants posing for photo
23. Mid of Sapunov, UPSOUND (Ukrainian) "Thank you all for the assistance. Glory to Ukraine." 
24. Close of Yuzvia holding a flag  UPSOUND (Ukrainian) "Glory to heroes"
25. Wide of participants cheering
26. Mid of Sapunov
27. Various of participants taking off on bicycles
STORYLINE:
Ukrainian war veterans, some of whom have lost limbs, joined professional triathlete Danylo Sapunov for a swimming event in Kyiv on Monday, the final day of Iron Week, which coincided with Ukraine’s Independence Day.

Some participants needed help putting on their swimming gear and making turns at the shore during the course, but their injuries did not stop them from taking part and completing the swim.

recentItems.title: México reanuda venta de ganado a EEUU bajo fuerte control y riesgo de la plaga del gusano barrenador
recentItems.description:
(24 Aug 2026) 
RESUMEN DE RESTRICCIONES:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Hermosillo, México - 17 de agosto de 2026
1. Varias tomas de becerros para exportación.
2. DECLARACIÓN (Español) Martín Ibarra, pequeño productor ganadero:
"Yo llegue a vender becerros por alrededor de 28 mil o 30 mil pesos por cabeza, antes del cierre de la frontera. Estas últimas ventas nos han salido alrededor de 16 o 17 mil pesos por animal. O sea, hay una reduccion de casi el 50 porciento. Redondeando yo creo que es un 40 porciento menos ingreso para nosotros, por el cierre de la frontera."

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Hermosillo, México - 17 de agosto de 2026
3. Varias tomas de vacas destinadas a la producción lechera.

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Hermosillo, México - 18 de agosto de 2026
4. DECLARACIÓN (Español) Juan Ochoa, presidente de la Unión Ganadera Regional de Sonora:
"En este momento lo que si tenemos son medicamentos que nos ayudan a controlar esto. Y eso es muy bueno. Nosotros siempre vimos una decision más política que sanitaria. Sanitariamente no hubiera habido tema. A la mosca del gusano barrenador ya la tuvimos hace ya 50 años y convivimos con ella." 
5. Varias tomas de ganado para exportación.
6. DECLARACIÓN (Español) Juan Ochoa, presidente de la Unión Ganadera Regional de Sonora:
 “Tengo entendido que empezaremos con 750 cabezas diarias. En este momento ese flujo es insuficiente. Nosotros necesitariamos exportar cuando menos de dos mil a tres mil cabezas diarias."
7. Varias tomas de ganado para exportación.
STORYLINE:
Los ganaderos del estado de Sonora, en el norte de México, se preparan para reanudar las exportaciones a Estados Unidos después de más de un año de interrupciones provocadas por la propagación del gusano barrenador del Nuevo Mundo, aunque advierten que el flujo inicial de ganado será demasiado reducido para eliminar rápidamente el rezago acumulado.

Estados Unidos comenzará a reabrir su frontera al ganado mexicano el 24 de agosto por el cruce de Douglas, Arizona, frente a Agua Prieta, Sonora.

La reapertura se produce después de que Estados Unidos suspendiera durante más de un año las importaciones de ganado mexicano debido a la propagación del gusano barrenador en México.

El gusano barrenador del Nuevo Mundo es una mosca parasitaria cuyas larvas se alimentan del tejido vivo de animales de sangre caliente, incluido el ganado, las mascotas y la fauna silvestre y, ocasionalmente, de seres humanos.

Estados Unidos prácticamente erradicó la plaga en las décadas de 1960 y 1970 mediante el uso de moscas estériles.

El brote fue detectado en México en noviembre de 2024 y desde entonces se ha propagado a 30 de los 32 estados del país.

También fue detectado recientemente en Sonora, donde el primer caso se reportó el miércoles en la comunidad de Munihuasa, cerca de los límites con Chihuahua y Sinaloa, estados donde las infecciones también han proliferado.

El parásito también llegó a Estados Unidos, donde se han reportado más de 30 casos en Texas y el sureste de Nuevo México.

El comercio ganadero se ha visto gravemente afectado. El año pasado, los ganaderos de Sonora se vieron obligados a vender sus animales en el mercado nacional tras la suspensión estadounidense, con frecuencia a precios inferiores a los que habrían obtenido al otro lado de la frontera.

Juan Ochoa, presidente de la Unión Ganadera Regional de Sonora, dijo que los productores lograron sobrellevar el cierre, en parte, porque la escasez de ganado mantuvo elevados los precios internos.




La reapertura forma parte de un esfuerzo más amplio de Estados Unidos y México para contener el parásito.

(24 Aug 2026)

MOFA Highlights                                      
Spokesperson: Lin Jian
Duration:  04 min 37 sec

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Beijing, China -  24 August 2026

1. What issues will the two sides discuss at tomorrow’s meeting of the Special Representatives on the China-India boundary question?

The meeting of Special Representatives on the China-India border issue is the main channel for negotiations on the border issue between the two countries, as well as an important platform for the two sides to communicate on matters of mutual concern. In August last year, the two sides successfully held the 24th special representatives' meeting, where they had candid and in-depth exchanges of views and reached a number of common understandings. At this meeting, the two sides will continue to have in-depth communication on the border issue and jointly safeguard peace and tranquility in the border areas in accordance with the understanding reached by the leaders of the two countries. Also, both sides will exchange views on bilateral relations and international and regional issues.

2. The U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has reportedly threatened to impose secondary sanctions on countries that trade with Iran. What is China’s comment?

Sanctions and pressure will not help resolve the issue. They will only exacerbate tensions and escalate the situation, which is in no one’s interest. China calls on all parties to remain rational and exercise restraint, avoid measures that could further intensify differences and conflicts and disrupt global economic development and financial stability, and return to the right track of dialogue and negotiations and a political solution as soon as possible. China will closely follow relevant developments and take necessary measures to safeguard its legitimate rights and interests.

3. Recently, some U.S. officials have attacked Chinese technology companies on social media, saying the high-risk technologies of relevant Chinese companies will create risks of espionage, cyberattacks and network disruptions, and urging the US partners in the Western Hemisphere to swiftly switch to trusted suppliers to protect their citizens and national sovereignty. What is China’s comment?

Such remarks fabricate facts and distort right and wrong. They are blatant technological bullying and unilateral coercion. China firmly opposes this.

4. Regarding the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region’s judiciary ruling, the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China (Hong Kong Alliance) and Lee Cheuk-yan, Albert Ho Chun-yan and Chow Hang-tung were guilty of inciting subversion of state power, some countries, including the US, and the European Union issued statements or expressed views voicing concern over the above verdicts. What is China’s response?


5. China and Indonesia have implemented some flagship projects under the high-level cooperation mechanism, such as the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway project. Now that China and Indonesia have established a comprehensive strategic dialogue mechanism, will the two countries promote the construction of more projects similar to the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway under this mechanism?

The China-Indonesia Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue Mechanism is an important measure for the two sides to implement the consensus reached by the leaders of the two countries. It aims to deepen practical cooperation in various fields, advance the building of a China-Indonesia community with a shared future, and bring tangible benefits to the people of both countries.

recentItems.title: La industria robótica china se muestra confiada a pesar de la prohibición de importación de EE.UU.
recentItems.description:
(24 Aug 2026) 
China Robots SP 
Source: ASSOCIATED PRESS
No additional restrictions beyond those terms outlined in your license agreement.

Vídeo de AP grabado por: Wayne Zhang y Wu Jia.

La industria robótica china se muestra confiada a pesar de la prohibición de importación de EE. UU.
————————————————————————————————————————-
ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Beijing, China - 19 de agosto de 2026 

China inauguró la Conferencia Mundial de Robots 2026 el 19 de agosto, con más de 300 empresas que exhibieron robots humanoides, máquinas industriales, robots de servicio y otras formas de inteligencia artificial. 

SOUNDBITE (Mandarín) Jiao Jichao, vicepresidente de UBTECH Robotics: 
“Un robot puede sustituir a dos trabajadores para completar las mismas tareas”, dijo este ejecutivo.

UBTECH, una de las principales empresas de robótica de China, presentó varios modelos, los que más atención atrajeron son los robots humanoides con rostros realistas, promocionados para el cuidado emocional.

Uno de ellos que puede hablar, girar el cuello y mover las manos, está disponible para compradores individuales. El precio: más de 24.000 dólares.

SOUNDBITE (Mandarín) Jiao Jichao, vicepresidente de UBTECH Robotics:
"Muchos países de todo el mundo tienen una gran demanda tanto de robots industriales como de robots personales comerciales, es un mercado global”.

La conferencia se celebra pocas semanas después de que la Comisión Federal de Comunicaciones de EE. UU. anunciara la prohibición de importar nuevos robots humanoides e inversores de potencia de fabricación extranjera, alegando riesgos para la seguridad nacional, en una medida dirigida contra China.

SOUNDBITE (Inglés) Ni Tao, consultor de la industria tecnológica: 

“Es indudable que se pierden fuentes de ingresos”, dijo este consultor.  “Pero podemos explorar otras opciones, vender a mercados alternativos: el Sudeste Asiático o Europa. Al fin y al cabo, siempre habrá compradores en el mundo, no solo en EE. UU.”.

Los organizadores señalan que se exhibirán unos 3.000 productos durante el evento, que dura cinco días.

ANNE MARIE GARCIA, ASSOCIATED PRESS

New York, 5 October 2016
1. Tilt up Kristen Stewart, pan to photographers and back

"Honestly, it was not like a tactical approach, you know what I mean? 4. SOUNDBITE (English) Kristen Stewart, actress - on being a workaholic:
"Oh yeah, I'm totally addicted man. Like I'm a crazy, compulsive, like I get super obsessed with stuff, you know, which is to a fault but it's served me well."
5. Medium of Kristen Stewart talking to reporter
6. SOUNDBITE (English) Kristen Stewart, actress - on what she's learned from directors Ang Lee and Kelly Reichardt:
"It's weird. I think I fall somewhere in between wanting to be really surgical and technical and in control of absolutely everything but at the same time I'm wanting to see something live and breathe and I think they both do that completely differently, but they both accomplish the same thing. I think they are both absolute geniuses when it comes to being composed and when it comes to being aware of something that we're not aware of. They see the invisible and they capture it and that's what I would like to do while making movies."
